items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: the saxophone player with Count Basie

ctx.x: In his book, "Jazz In the Movies", by David Meeker, they have a listing of Belle of the Nineties and there is a picture from it, and you're in the picture; I guess it was probably taken on the set, and it said it was at Paramount Studios in 1934. And it says it's one of the classic Mae West vehicles in which she portrays a tough 19th Century showgirl in love with a young boxer. Duke Ellington was all and sometimes part of his orchestra, provides the backing off and on screen for the songs, When A St. Louis Woman…
Uh huh. That was his name -- the saxophone player with Count Basie. His name didn't get in the listing. Marshal Royal, whose name doesn't get into the listing.
He was what? Instead of Toby?
